Statue_of_Liberty.name: Statue of Liberty
Statue_of_Liberty.statistics_text_present:
-Height: 93 m
-Visitors: 3.2 million/year
-Material: Copper
-UNESCO Site since: 1984
-Opened: October 28, 1886
Statue_of_Liberty.statistics_text_past:
-Gift: From France to USA
-Architect: Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi
-Original color: Dull brown (copper)
-Engineering: Gustave Eiffel framework
-Symbolism: Enlightenment and Freedom
Statue_of_Liberty.past_comparison_summary: From a shiny copper gift to a green-patina symbol of American freedom and democracy.

Golden_Gate_Bridge.name: Golden Gate Bridge
Golden_Gate_Bridge.description: Famous suspension bridge in San Francisco
Golden_Gate_Bridge.statistics_text_present:
-Length: 2,737 m
-Color: International Orange
-Daily traffic: ~110,000 cars
-Towers height: 227 m
-Completed: 1937
Golden_Gate_Bridge.statistics_text_past:
-Built: 1933–1937
-Engineer: Joseph Strauss
-Style: Art Deco elements
-Materials: 88,000 tons of steel
-History: Replaced ferry service
Golden_Gate_Bridge.past_comparison_summary: A marvel of 1930s engineering that became San Francisco's most iconic silhouette.

Lincoln_Memorial.name: Lincoln Memorial
Lincoln_Memorial.statistics_text_present:
-Height: 30 m
-Columns: 36 Doric columns
-Statue height: 5.8 m
-Visitors: 7 million/year
-Style: Greek Doric temple
Lincoln_Memorial.statistics_text_past:
-Built: 1914–1922
-Architect: Henry Bacon
-Statue Sculptor: Daniel Chester French
-Site: Reclaimed swampland
-Dedicated: May 30, 1922
Lincoln_Memorial.past_comparison_summary: A solemn Greek-inspired temple rising from marshland to honor the legacy of national unity.

Eiffel_Tower.name: Eiffel Tower
Eiffel_Tower.statistics_text_present:
-Height: 330 m
-Visitors: 6 million/year
-Floors: 3 accessible levels
-Maintenance: Repainted every 7 years
-Status: Global icon of France
Eiffel_Tower.statistics_text_past:
-Built: 1887–1889
-Occasion: 1889 World's Fair
-Architect: Stephen Sauvestre
-Engineer: Gustave Eiffel
-Controversy: Initially hated by many artists
Eiffel_Tower.past_comparison_summary: From a 'useless' temporary exhibition piece to the global symbol of French elegance.

Louvre_Museum.name: Louvre Museum
Louvre_Museum.statistics_text_present:
-Visitors: 9 million/year
-Objects: ~38,000 on display
-Pyramid addition: 1989
-Surface: 72,735 m²
-Famous work: Mona Lisa
Louvre_Museum.statistics_text_past:
-Origins: Medieval fortress (12th C)
-Rebuilt: As royal palace (16th C)
-Royal use: Primary residence until Versailles
-Museum Opening: 1793
-Architecture: French Renaissance and Baroque
Louvre_Museum.past_comparison_summary: Evolution from a defensive medieval fortress to the world's most visited art sanctuary.

Mont_Saint_Michel.name: Mont Saint-Michel
Mont_Saint_Michel.description: Tidal island and abbey in Normandy
Mont_Saint_Michel.statistics_text_present:
-Population: ~30 residents
-Visitors: 3 million/year
-UNESCO Site since: 1979
-Access: New bridge completed in 2014
-Tides: Highest in Europe
Mont_Saint_Michel.statistics_text_past:
-Founded: Abbey started in 8th C
-Defense: Survived Hundred Years' War
-Prison: Used as jail during French Revolution
-Strategic: Fortified island village
-Causeway: Original was a tidal path
Mont_Saint_Michel.past_comparison_summary: A spiritual island fortress that survived centuries of conflict to become a tourist jewel.

Colosseum.name: Colosseum
Colosseum.statistics_text_present:
-Capacity: ~50,000 people
-Status: UNESCO World Heritage
-Material: Travertine, tuff, and brick-faced concrete
-Visitors: 7 million/year
-Symbol: Iconic Rome landmark
Colosseum.statistics_text_past:
-Completed: 80 AD (Vespasian/Titus)
-Games: Gladiatorial contests and mock sea battles
-Facade: Originally covered in marble
-Damage: Earthquakes and stone robbers
-Hypogeum: Underground tunnel network
Colosseum.past_comparison_summary: The transformation of the Roman Empire's grandest arena into a preserved symbol of antiquity.

Leaning_Tower_of_Pisa.name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
Leaning_Tower_of_Pisa.statistics_text_present:
-Height: 56 m
-Lean: ~3.97 degrees
-Weight: ~14,500 tons
-Steps: 294 or 296
-Stabilized: Major restoration in 1990-2001
Leaning_Tower_of_Pisa.statistics_text_past:
-Construction: Started in 1173
-Problem: Began leaning during 2nd floor construction
-Soil: Unstable clay, mud, and sand
-Duration: Took 199 years to finish
-Architect: Unknown (attributed to Bonanno Pisano)
Leaning_Tower_of_Pisa.past_comparison_summary: An accidental architectural error that became one of the most famous landmarks in the world.

Pantheon.name: Pantheon
Pantheon.statistics_text_present:
-Dome: World's largest unreinforced concrete dome
-Diameter: 43.3 m
-Status: State-owned church (Basilica)
-Tombs: Raphael and Italian Kings
-Occasion: Still active for religious services
Pantheon.statistics_text_past:
-Commissioned: Marcus Agrippa (original)
-Rebuilt: Hadrian in ~126 AD
-Purpose: Temple for all Roman gods
-Conversion: Consecrated as church in 609 AD
-Oculus: The only source of natural light
Pantheon.past_comparison_summary: An architectural masterpiece that has remained in continuous use for nearly 2,000 years.

Sagrada_Familia.name: Sagrada Familia
Sagrada_Familia.statistics_text_present:
-Height: 172.5 m
-Visitors: 8–10 million/year
-Capacity: ~15,000 people
-Avg. visit: 2.5 h
-Energy: self-sufficient
Sagrada_Familia.statistics_text_past:
-Started: 1882
-Architect: Antoni Gaudí
-Style: Modernisme
-Original budget: Humble donations
-Status in 1900: Only Nativity facade started
Sagrada_Familia.past_comparison_summary: A transition from a visionary construction site to a world-renowned architectural masterpiece.

Plaza_Mayor_de_Salamanca.name: Plaza Mayor de Salamanca
Plaza_Mayor_de_Salamanca.statistics_text_present:
-Style: Churrigueresque Baroque
-Surface: 6,400 m²
-Medallions: 88 carved faces
-Arches: 88 semicircular arches
-Tradition: Meeting point for students
Plaza_Mayor_de_Salamanca.statistics_text_past:
-Built: 1729–1755
-Architect: Alberto Churriguera
-Original use: Bullfights until 1854
-Material: Villamayor stone
-Royal support: Philip V
Plaza_Mayor_de_Salamanca.past_comparison_summary: Evolution from a multifunctional royal square and bullring to the social heart of university life.

Cathedral_of_Santiago_de_Compostela.name: Cathedral of Santiago de Compostela
Cathedral_of_Santiago_de_Compostela.statistics_text_present:
-Pilgrims: >300,000/year
-Main attraction: Botafumeiro
-Style: Romanesque, Gothic, Baroque
-Botafumeiro weight: 53 kg
-Botafumeiro speed: 68 km/h
Cathedral_of_Santiago_de_Compostela.statistics_text_past:
-Consecrated: 1211
-Pórtico de la Gloria: Master Mateo
-Origin: Discovery of St. James tomb
-Expansion: Baroque facade (18th century)
-Defense: Fortress-like towers
Cathedral_of_Santiago_de_Compostela.past_comparison_summary: From a medieval defensive fortress and pilgrimage site to a Baroque religious icon.

Alhambra_de_Granada.name: Alhambra de Granada
Alhambra_de_Granada.statistics_text_present:
-Visitors: 2.7 million/year
-Surface: 140,000 m²
-UNESCO Site since: 1984
-Gardens: Generalife
-Status: Most visited in Spain
Alhambra_de_Granada.statistics_text_past:
-Started: 1238 (Nasrid Dynasty)
-Founder: Muhammad I
-Style: Moorish Architecture
-Capture: 1492 by Catholic Monarchs
-Addition: Palace of Charles V (1527)
Alhambra_de_Granada.past_comparison_summary: The transformation of a Nasrid royal citadel into a Spanish Renaissance monumental complex.

Palacio_Real_de_Madrid.name: Palacio Real de Madrid
Palacio_Real_de_Madrid.statistics_text_present:
-Floor area: 135,000 m²
-Rooms: 3,418
-Status: Largest in Europe by floor area
-Visitors: 1.5 million/year
-Collections: Stradivarius Palatinos
Palacio_Real_de_Madrid.statistics_text_past:
-Built: 1738–1755
-Site: Former Moorish Alcázar
-Fire: Destroyed old palace in 1734
-Architects: Juvarra & Sacchetti
-First Royal: Charles III in 1764
Palacio_Real_de_Madrid.past_comparison_summary: The reconstruction after the 1734 fire, replacing the old Alcázar with Europe's largest palace.
